section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yud-Hei represents the concealed intellect (mochin) and Vav-Hei represents the revealed emotions (middos), because intellect is for oneself while emotions are for another, and this distinction applies even to the essence of these faculties.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in Likkutei Torah,
that Yud-Hei are the hidden things and Vav-Hei are the revealed things.
And the explanation is,
that Yud-Hei are the intellect (mochin) and Vav-Hei are the emotions (middos)
(as above),
and among the distinctions between intellect and emotions is,
that intellect is for oneself and emotions are for another
(as will be explained at length below),
and correspondingly above,
the emotions are for the sake of the worlds and the intellect is above the worlds,
therefore,
the emotions are in a state of revelation to another,
revealed,
and the intellect is in concealment from another,
hidden.
And now, that intellect is hidden and emotions are revealed,
the intent in this is,
that the entire concept of emotions,
even the emotions in the heart
(before one reveals them to another),
are in the category of revealed,
and correspondingly on the other hand,
the entire concept of intellect
(even after one reveals his understanding to another)
is in the category of hidden.
And the explanation is,
that this — that emotions pertain to another —
is not only regarding the activity of the emotions but also regarding the emotions themselves.
For example, the attribute of kindness, whose essence is to bestow good to another,
and without another,
the concept of kindness does not apply.
And although it is explained in many places
that this — that emotions are impossible without another — is specifically regarding the activity of the emotions,
but not so the arousal of the emotions
(and all the more so the essence of the emotions)
can exist even without another,
as with Avraham Avinu who was distressed that there were no guests,
this — that he was distressed that it was not in his ability to bestow — is because the attribute of kindness was in a state of arousal within him
(even when there was no other),
but this is specifically when there exists in the world
(another)
upon whom to bestow kindness,
but if there were no other found in the world upon whom to bestow,
the arousal of the attribute of kindness could not exist,
and furthermore,
then even the concept of kindness would not apply
(the essence of the attribute),
for the concept of kindness is to bestow good to another.
And to add,
from this very thing — that Avraham Avinu was distressed that he had no one upon whom to bestow —
it is proven,
that the bestowal
(in actuality)
to another also pertains to the attribute of kindness itself.
For distress is when there is some lack,
and this — that Avraham was distressed that it was not in his ability to bestow — is because the concept of kindness is to bestow,
and when the bestowal is not actualized,
there is a lack in the perfection of the attribute of kindness.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as emotions inherently pertain to another, so too intellect is inherently for oneself, and even the activity of intellect does not require another, as one can contemplate alone and solitude aids clarity.
section.t: And now, just as with emotions,
even the emotions themselves pertain to another,
so too on the other hand with intellect,
that this — that intellect is for oneself, above connection to another — is not only regarding the intellect itself,
for the concept of intellect is for oneself
[and unlike emotions,
whose concept
(even the concept of the emotions themselves)
is to bestow to another],
but rather, even for the activity of intellect there is no need for another,
for even when a person is by himself
(without another)
he can contemplate intellectual concepts.
And although through bestowal to another an addition is made in the intellect,
and "from my students more than from all,"
this is specifically regarding an addition in intellect,
but the essence of contemplation
(even actual contemplation)
can exist even without another.
For even when there is no one upon whom to bestow, one can contemplate great and deep intellectual concepts.
And on the contrary,
in order to arrive at a matter of intellect and to understand it clearly,
sometimes another person disturbs.
Therefore most of the wise men would seclude themselves.
And this is what our sages said,
that the Sanhedrin would debate and deliberate all night,
and Rashi explained: each one by himself,
for in order to arrive at the truth of a logical reasoning, it is specifically when one contemplates by himself.
And also according to the explanation of the Rambam,
that each one would debate and deliberate with his partner
— this is specifically with his partner,
and not all together.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that emotions are revealed because their essence is to bestow to another, while intellect is hidden because even when revealed to another, its essence remains concealed and its revelation is not intrinsic to its nature.
section.t: And this is that intellect is hidden and emotions are revealed,
for emotions,
since their concept is to bestow to another,
are in the category of revelation,
except that when they are in the heart, the actual revelation has not yet come.
And intellect,
since its concept is that it is for oneself, above connection to another,
therefore,
even when one reveals his intellect to another,
it is in the category of concealment.
And there are two aspects in this.
For the intellect that is revealed to another is not like the intellect that one contemplated in himself
[and as explained in many places,
the bestowal of intellect to another is through the intermediary of the emotions],
and thus,
the essence of the intellect
(as it is in itself)
remains in concealment.
And there is another aspect in this,
that even the level of intellect that is revealed to another,
its revelation to another is not because its concept is revelation to another,
for the entirety of intellect
(even the level of intellect that is revealed to another)
is a matter for itself,
rather, it reveals to another the matters that are within itself
(which are above revelation to another).
